data.long_meaning: Musir is a name derived from the Arabic word 'musirah', which means 'a source of joy' or 'delight'. It is mentioned in the Quran as one of the names for Paradise, where the people will find eternal joy and happiness. The name Musir carries the meaning “Delight, Joy” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Musir usually hope their child will grow to embody delight, joy and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Khaldun's 'The Muqaddimah' (1377-1406 AD), vol. 1, p. 226. The name Musir carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun describes the Maghrib, a region in North Africa, as being divided into several kingdoms, one of which was the Kingdom of Musir. He mentions that it was originally part of the Almohad Empire, but broke away and became independent in the late 13th century.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's 'Al-Mawā'īz wa l-ī'tibār bi-Dhayl al-Iḥtīār' (1401-1442 AD), vol. 2, p. 147. The name Musir carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Maqrizi writes about the city of Tunis and its various rulers. He mentions that during the Hafsid period (1236-1574 AD), there was a king named Abu Abd Allah Muhammad II who ruled the Kingdom of Musir. He was known for his military conquests and the construction of several notable buildings in Tunis.
